title: Knowledge Check 11 - Lessons 51-55
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 51-55 - Testing, Deployment, and Maintenance | Governance and Observability. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A partner must ship an Agentforce agent to customer orgs as a package. What is the correct approach?
options: Create an agent template, include the template in the package, and create a new agent from that template in the target org
Package the agent record directly, since an agent is metadata
Export the agent's testing cases and import them into each target org
Deploy the agent user record inside the package so the agent runs immediately
questions.explanation: The agent itself cannot be packaged directly, so the template is the unit you include in the package and you instantiate an agent from it in the target org.

questions.question: After deploying a template to a target org, what still has to happen before the agent is usable there?
options: Nothing, because deploying the template deploys the agent with it
Retrieve the agent metadata a second time so the actions resolve
Create the agent from the template, name it, and select or create its agent user record
Convert the template back into a legacy Bot before it can run
questions.explanation: Promoting a template moves a blueprint, so the target org still creates the agent from the template and supplies the agent's identity and its user record.

questions.question: Which statement about the relationship between a template and an agent type is correct?
options: A template can belong to several agent types at once
A type can be associated with many templates, but a template is associated with exactly one type, so the target org must have that type
A template has no relationship to an agent type at all
Any template can create an agent from any type as long as metadata is enabled
questions.explanation: A template is a child of exactly one agent type, so creating an agent from it in the target org requires that type and its permissions to be present.

questions.question: A team must stand up the same employee agent in three identically configured orgs. All three run the same flows and share the same agent type. What is the right approach?
options: Rebuild the agent by hand in each org to avoid any metadata risk
Reuse the template: deploy it with its dependencies, then create the agent from the template in each org
Package the agent record directly so it installs without an instantiation step
Skip the template and copy the agent user record between orgs instead
questions.explanation: When the blueprint matches and the target orgs share the agent type and dependencies, reusing the template is the efficient path, and each org then creates the agent from it.

questions.question: A target org does not have the agent type that a source template depends on. What is the best approach?
options: Deploy the template anyway, because a template can attach to any type
Retrieve the type from the source org as metadata and force it into the target
Rebuild in the target org using a template whose agent type is available there, since a template attaches to exactly one type
Package the agent itself directly, which bypasses the type requirement
questions.explanation: A template is a child of exactly one agent type and cannot attach elsewhere, so when the type is absent the correct move is to rebuild against a type the target org actually supports.

questions.question: A team ships a template, several orgs build agents from it, and later the team edits the template to add a new subagent. What happens to the agents already built?
options: Nothing changes until those agents are re-created from the template, because edits reach only newly created agents
Every agent inherits the new subagent automatically on the next conversation
The existing agents fail validation and must be redeployed
The template edit is rejected while built agents reference it
questions.explanation: Template changes apply only to agents newly created from the template, so agents already built keep their original asset set until they are rebuilt from the updated template.

questions.question: A consultant must correct wording in an agent that is running in production without taking the live version out of service. What is the correct sequence?
options: Edit the live agent in place, then save, because saving updates the active version
Create a new version, edit and test it, commit it, then activate it, which deactivates the currently active version
Deactivate the agent, edit it, and reactivate it under the same version number
Commit the active version again with the fix, because recommitting overwrites the snapshot
questions.explanation: The change must go into a new version that is tested and committed before activation, and activating it retires the old active version automatically.

questions.question: What does committing an agent version do?
options: It publishes the version to every connected channel immediately
It merges the version into the active version's draft history
It deletes the previous version from Agentforce Builder
It saves a snapshot of the version to metadata and makes it available to activate, after which the version can no longer be edited
questions.explanation: Commit writes a frozen snapshot to metadata so the version can be activated, and the freeze is what stops you editing it afterward.

questions.question: Which statement about agent versions is correct?
options: Only one version of an agent can be active at a time, and activating a new version deactivates the prior active version
Multiple versions can be active at once so you can A/B test in production
A committed version can still be edited until it is activated
A draft version can be activated before it is committed
questions.explanation: The platform allows a single active version, so activating a new one automatically retires the old one.

questions.question: A team turns on Agent Analytics but the dashboards never show any sessions. What is the most likely cause?
options: The agent has no connected channel
Agentforce Session Tracing was not enabled, and no observability tool has data until it is
The Tableau Next dashboard needs a manual refresh each morning
The agent type does not support analytics
questions.explanation: Session Tracing must be enabled first because every other observability tool draws on the session record it captures.

questions.question: Three days after a launch, an operator filters the Sessions and Intents page and finds no intents at all. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The sessions were deleted by the retention policy
The agent is not connected to any channel
The operator lacks the permission to see intents
No intent group has yet reached the cluster threshold, because intents are generated daily and clustered weekly
questions.explanation: Intents are generated daily and clustered weekly, and a group with too few matching intents does not form a cluster, so an empty list early in a launch is expected.

questions.question: Where would an operator set a threshold that notifies the team when the agent's error rate breaches an acceptable level?
options: In Agent Health, reached from Agentforce Studio under Alerts
In the Agent Analytics Effectiveness tab
In Setup under Agentforce Session Tracing
In the Agent Optimization Sessions and Intents filters
questions.explanation: Agent Health under Alerts is where you create alerts and thresholds on Health metrics such as Error Rate, latency, and session duration.

questions.question: Which metric is defined as the share of sessions that ended without escalation to a support representative or another agent?
options: Success Rate
Engagement Rate
Deflection Rate
Abandonment Rate
questions.explanation: Deflection Rate is the share of sessions that ended without escalation, which is distinct from abandonment and engagement.

questions.question: A response reads fluently and answers the question, but it cites the wrong knowledge article. Which Quality Score signal points at this?
options: Low Context Relevance, because the agent retrieved the wrong source for the question
Low Adherence Response Rate, because the agent ignored its instructions
High Abandonment Rate, because the user disengaged
Low Success Rate, because an action step errored
questions.explanation: Context Relevance scores whether the correct source was retrieved, so a fluent answer grounded on the wrong document shows there.

questions.question: You see a metric trend on the Effectiveness tab and need to know which subagent or action drove it. Where do you go?
options: The Overview tab, which summarizes every dimension
The Session Outcome stack bar chart
The Usage tab
Performance Insights, which breaks a metric down by subagent, intent, or action
questions.explanation: Performance Insights provides the breakdowns by subagent, intent, or action that localize a trend before you open sessions.
